subject: Production latency spike — Orion Analytics (inferencing throughput impact)
messages:
From: Alex Foster <afoster@orionanalytics.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: samantha.chu@orionanalytics.com, procurement@orionanalytics.com
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike — urgent assistance

Karthik / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in inference latency and error rate across our production endpoints at ~08:50 PDT —  p95 latency jumped from ~230ms to ~2.1s and error-rate (5xx) climbed to ~4.2%. Throughput dropped as retries kicked in; our downstream jobs are backing up. This is impacting our BI pipelines and customer-facing features.

Attached is a quick KPI snapshot (last 6h) and a short annotated log export. Can you confirm whether this is a model-serving/regression issue or something on the routing layer? We need an immediate estimate on ETA to stabilize and a contact for an urgent bridge.

Impact:
- Multiple customers seeing degraded response times (observability flagged high error spike)
- 30% of requests now retrying (client-side), increasing cost and queuing
- Affected routes: orion-prod-embedding-v2, orion-prod-chat-1

Please escalate.

—Alex
Alex Foster
Head of Platform, Orion Analytics
afoster@orionanalytics.com

Attachments: orion_kpi_snapshot_20270424.xlsx (spreadsheet), svc-call-recording-20270424.mp3 (audio)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Foster <afoster@orionanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com, samantha.chu@orionanalytics.com
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — urgent assistance

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts.

We're standing up an immediate incident bridge and triage. Core ask: preserve the logs you attached (we may request additional traces). Our initial plan:
1) Triage to determine whether this is model/kernel change, routing, or resource saturation.
2) If routing/capacity, shift traffic to a fallback variant and scale Dedicated pool.
3) If a model regression, rollback to pinned model snapshot for the affected routes.

I have looped in:
- Marissa Cole (SRE lead) — owning triage and logs
- Laura Bennett (CS lead) — customer comms and exec sync
- Rishi Malhotra (runtime) — kernel/quantization checks
- Evelyn Hart (ops) — Dedicated/GPU pool scaling & capacity

War-room details: we'll host a short bridge at 10:00 PDT; I'll send an invite in 5. If you prefer a private VPC-only postmortem, flag that now.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — urgent assistance

On it — quick diagnostic notes from the first 20 minutes of triage:

- Observability: metrics confirm p95 spike and 5xx uptick across the two routes Alex called out. Error traces point to transient OOMs followed by request retries in the serving tier (seen on GPU nodes a-3, a-7).
- Kernel/quantization: Rishi, can you check whether the new quantization profile rolled last night is affecting KV cache propagation?
- Scaling: Evelyn, we'll need immediate scale-out to the Dedicated pool with burst capacity enablement; please start the ops runbook for autoscale override.

Action items (owners):
- Marissa: collect full traces and correlate with kernel logs (10:15)
- Rishi: validate current model variant + kernel selection; prepare rollback candidate (10:20)
- Evelyn: enable burst scaling and monitor queue length (10:10)
- Laura: prepare an external status note for Orion execs (draft based on my notes) (10:20)

I'll post updates on the bridge.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Foster <afoster@orionanalytics.com>, samantha.chu@orionanalytics.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — urgent assistance

Alex / Samantha — thank you for flagging. We just finished an initial investigation on the bridge and wanted to share a short status update for your execs while we work on remediation. Please feel free to adapt and share.

External status (internal draft):
- What happened: Starting ~08:50 PDT, we observed increased latency and error rate on two inference routes. Early traces indicate transient OOMs in the serving tier triggering retries and queue buildup.
- Impact: Elevated p95 (from ~230ms to ~2.1s) and a 4.2% 5xx error rate affecting embedding and chat routes; some downstream batch jobs are delayed.
- Immediate remediation steps underway: scaling Dedicated capacity (burst), validating current quantization/profile, and preparing a rollback to the previous model snapshot.
- ETA & next update: We expect initial stabilization within 45–60 minutes; we'll update within 30 minutes or sooner if there's a material change.
- Point of contact: Karthik Iyer (SE) and Marissa Cole (SRE lead) on the incident bridge.

We will run a follow-up exec summary after stabilization with a root cause hypothesis and next steps for preventing recurrence.

Laura Bennett
Customer Success Director, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: warroom-invite.ics (bridge at 10:00 PDT)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Foster <afoster@orionanalytics.com>, Samantha Chu <samantha.chu@orionanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Status update — Orion production incident (11:00 PDT)

Alex / Samantha — quick external-facing update following the war-room: 

- What we've done so far:
  • Enabled Dedicated pool burst scaling and disabled autoscale cap for the affected clusters (Evelyn)
  • Rolled traffic to a pinned model snapshot for orion-prod-embedding-v2 (Rishi) — initial sanity checks pass
  • Cleared KV cache and warmed prefix caches for high-volume routes (Marissa)

- Current state (11:00 PDT):
  • p95 latency reduced from ~2.1s to ~420ms across the affected routes
  • Error-rate down from 4.2% to ~0.8% and trending down
  • Queue lengths decreasing; throughput returning toward baseline but not fully recovered yet

- Next steps (short):
  1) Continue monitoring for the next 60 minutes; if stable, we'll scale back burst capacity gradually.
  2) Postmortem with timeline and root-cause hypothesis within 48 hours.
  3) Propose short remediation: pin model variants for production traffic windows and run a targeted kernel regression test across our Dedicated pools.

We understand the customer impact and will escalate to executive leadership at Orion if you prefer. We will also prepare a credit proposal if the final postmortem shows preventable SLA impact.

Please confirm if you need immediate exec-briefing (we can loop in our VP of Product and your exec sponsor).

Regards,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Subject: Re: Production latency spike — urgent assistance

Karthik / team — thanks for the rapid response and the update. The metrics you shared are encouraging and we can see improvements on our end. A couple of asks: 

1) Please prepare a formal incident notice for our execs (CRO + CTO) with timeline and SLO impact (we will need this for our internal postmortem).
2) We expect Redwood to propose a remedial credit if the postmortem shows missed SLOs; please send a preliminary framework.
3) Keep procurement in the loop — we may request an emergency amendment if we need temporary higher capacity for a week.

If you think exec escalation from Redwood would help, go ahead and loop your VP; we will do the same here.

Appreciate the fast mobilization.

—Alex
Alex Foster
Head of Platform, Orion Analytics
afoster@orionanalytics.com
